experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Epoxidation of the Enecarbamates 1 with Dimethyldioxirane (GP1) The enecarbamate 1 (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in acetone (30 mL) and 0.50 g of molecular sieves (5 Å) was added under an argon-gas atmosphere. The solution was cooled to 0 °C and after 10 min magnetic stirring, 1.0 equiv. of dimethyldioxirane (0.09 M in acetone) was added. The reaction mixture was allowed to warm up to ca. 20 °C while stirring, and the reaction progress was monitored for the presence of DMD by iodometry (KI/HOAC). After complete DMD consumption (the reaction times are given for the individual cases), the reaction mixture was centrifuged to remove the molecular sieves, the sieves were washed with acetone (2x15 mL) and centrifuged again. From the combined centrifugates, the acetone was removed (20 °C, 30 mbar) and the epoxide 2 was obtained as only product. The epoxides 2 were too labile for purification by silica-gel chromatography, and were characterized by their 1H-and 13C-NMR spectra and exact mass determination on the diastereomeric mixture [except epoxide 2a, which decomposed completely already at room temperature (ca. 20 °C) in a couple of hours]. The diastereomeric ratio was determined by 1H-NMR analysis directly on the crude reaction mixture, through integration of the areas under the characteristic NMR signals. In the case of nearly 1:1 mixtures of the diastereomers, COSY, HMBC and HMQC experiments were carried out for rigorous assignment. For the configurational assignment of the individual diastereomers, see General Procedure GP3. The epoxides 2b-d persist as neat solids for several months at -20 °C, but they readily decompose in solution in the presence of acid traces at room temperature (ca. 20 °C). For this reason, after formation, the labile epoxides must be immediately worked up to remove the solvent and the molecular sieves to minimize decomposition. Reactions were performed at ambient temperature under argon atmosphere unless otherwise indicated. All reactions were run in at least triplicate, and the data reported represent the average of these reactions. The competitive epoxidations of cis- and trans-stilbenes and of cyclooctene and trans-stilbene in protic solvent were carried out as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3OH/CH2Cl2 (3:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (0.15 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3OH and CH2Cl2 (3:1). The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC. Product yields were determined by comparison against standard curves. The reaction conditions in aprotic solvent were as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3CN/CH2Cl2 (1:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (1.0 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3CN and CH2Cl2 (1:1). The competitive epoxidations studied with H2O2 were carried out in the presence of 5-chloro-1-methylimidazole (0.1 mmol), since the epoxidation of olefins by iron porphyrin complexes and H2O2 in aprotic solvent did not yield epoxide products in the absence of the imidazole.23 The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC with known authentic samples. Cyclooctene oxide, yield 10%; trans-stilbene oxide, yield 87%.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Epoxidation of the Enecarbamates 1 with Dimethyldioxirane (GP1) The enecarbamate 1 (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in acetone (30 mL) and 0.50 g of molecular sieves (5 Å) was added under an argon-gas atmosphere. The solution was cooled to 0 °C and after 10 min magnetic stirring, 1.0 equiv. of dimethyldioxirane (0.09 M in acetone) was added. The reaction mixture was allowed to warm up to ca. 20 °C while stirring, and the reaction progress was monitored for the presence of DMD by iodometry (KI/HOAC). After complete DMD consumption (the reaction times are given for the individual cases), the reaction mixture was centrifuged to remove the molecular sieves, the sieves were washed with acetone (2x15 mL) and centrifuged again. From the combined centrifugates, the acetone was removed (20 °C, 30 mbar) and the epoxide 2 was obtained as only product. The epoxides 2 were too labile for purification by silica-gel chromatography, and were characterized by their 1H-and 13C-NMR spectra and exact mass determination on the diastereomeric mixture [except epoxide 2a, which decomposed completely already at room temperature (ca. 20 °C) in a couple of hours]. The diastereomeric ratio was determined by 1H-NMR analysis directly on the crude reaction mixture, through integration of the areas under the characteristic NMR signals. In the case of nearly 1:1 mixtures of the diastereomers, COSY, HMBC and HMQC experiments were carried out for rigorous assignment. For the configurational assignment of the individual diastereomers, see General Procedure GP3. The epoxides 2b-d persist as neat solids for several months at -20 °C, but they readily decompose in solution in the presence of acid traces at room temperature (ca. 20 °C). For this reason, after formation, the labile epoxides must be immediately worked up to remove the solvent and the molecular sieves to minimize decomposition. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Catalytic Competitive Epoxidations in Protic and Aprotic Solvents. Reactions were performed at ambient temperature under argon atmosphere unless otherwise indicated. The reaction mixture was allowed to warm up to ca. 20 °C while stirring, and the reaction progress was monitored for the presence of DMD by iodometry (KI/HOAC). The diastereomeric ratio was determined by 1H-NMR analysis directly on the crude reaction mixture, through integration of the areas under the characteristic NMR signals. In the case of nearly 1:1 mixtures of the diastereomers, COSY, HMBC and HMQC experiments were carried out for rigorous assignment. For the configurational assignment of the individual diastereomers, see General Procedure GP3. The epoxides 2b-d persist as neat solids for several months at -20 °C, but they readily decompose in solution in the presence of acid traces at room temperature (ca. 20 °C).
